## Overview

With several types of host the next-generation matrix has several states-at-infection.
This vignette works through section 2.2 of Diekmann et al. (2010), two host categories
with a general `2 × 2` closed form, then the special case of separable mixing (rank one),
non-interacting strains (block structure, `R₀` is a maximum), and finally an
age-structured model with a contact matrix where no closed form exists and `R₀` is
evaluated numerically.

## Two host categories

```{julia}
using ReproductiveNumbers, ModelingToolkit, Symbolics, LinearAlgebra
using ModelingToolkit: t_nounits as t, D_nounits as D

@parameters β₁₁ β₁₂ β₂₁ β₂₂ ν₁ ν₂ γ₁ γ₂ μ N₁ N₂
@variables S₁(t) S₂(t) E₁(t) E₂(t) I₁(t) I₂(t)
N = N₁ + N₂
eqs = [D(S₁) ~ μ * N₁ - β₁₁ * S₁ * I₁ / N - β₁₂ * S₁ * I₂ / N - μ * S₁,
    D(S₂) ~ μ * N₂ - β₂₁ * S₂ * I₁ / N - β₂₂ * S₂ * I₂ / N - μ * S₂,
    D(E₁) ~ β₁₁ * S₁ * I₁ / N + β₁₂ * S₁ * I₂ / N - (ν₁ + μ) * E₁,
    D(E₂) ~ β₂₁ * S₂ * I₁ / N + β₂₂ * S₂ * I₂ / N - (ν₂ + μ) * E₂,
    D(I₁) ~ ν₁ * E₁ - (γ₁ + μ) * I₁,
    D(I₂) ~ ν₂ * E₂ - (γ₂ + μ) * I₂]
two_host = complete(System(eqs, t; name = :two_host))
ngm = next_generation_matrix(two_host, [E₁, E₂, I₁, I₂])
```

The transmission matrix is `4 × 4` but only the `E` rows are non-zero, so `K` is `2 × 2`:

```{julia}
ngm.K
```

For an irreducible non-negative `2 × 2` matrix the dominant eigenvalue is
`(tr K + √((K₁₁ − K₂₂)² + 4 K₁₂ K₂₁)) / 2`, equation (2.12) of the paper (the discriminant
is written in a form that makes it manifestly non-negative):

```{julia}
R0 = basic_reproduction_number(ngm)
```

## A readable form

The entries of `K` are products of three kinds of quantity: transmission rates, mean sojourn
times and transition probabilities. `abbreviate` names them (`τ_x`, `p_x_y` for the
transition from `x` to `y`, and with `transmissions = true` also `T_y_x` for `T[y, x]`), and
lists the definitions when the result is printed:

```{julia}
ab = abbreviate(ngm; transmissions = true)
```

The closed form then reads like the paper's derivation:

```{julia}
basic_reproduction_number(ab)
```

and can be expanded back or evaluated with the original parameter values:

```{julia}
symbolic_isequal(expand_definitions(ab, basic_reproduction_number(ab)), R0)
```

Your own quantities work too. Each definition is solved for one parameter, which is then
eliminated from the matrices:

```{julia}
@parameters R₁ R₂
ab2 = abbreviate(
    ngm, [R₁ => β₁₁ * ν₁ / ((ν₁ + μ) * (γ₁ + μ)), R₂ => β₂₂ * ν₂ / ((ν₂ + μ) * (γ₂ + μ))])
ab2.K
```

## Separable mixing

If `β_ij = a_i b_j`, `K` has rank one and `R₀` collapses to the trace (section 2.2 of the
paper, and the small-domain construction of section 3.3). The package detects this automatically:

```{julia}
@parameters a₁ a₂ b₁ b₂
sep = Dict(β₁₁ => a₁ * b₁, β₁₂ => a₁ * b₂, β₂₁ => a₂ * b₁, β₂₂ => a₂ * b₂)
K_sep = substitute.(ngm.K, Ref(sep))
(symbolic_isequal(det(K_sep), 0), spectral_radius(K_sep))
```

## Non-interacting strains

Two strains that confer complete cross-immunity and never interact give a block-diagonal
`K`; the spectrum of a block-triangular matrix is the union of the spectra of its diagonal
blocks, so `R₀` is the larger of the two strain-specific values. The package finds the
irreducible blocks (strongly connected components of the pattern of non-zero entries) and
returns a symbolic `max`:

```{julia}
@parameters βa βb γa γb Nₛ
@variables S(t) Ia(t) Ib(t) R(t)
strains = complete(System(
    [D(S) ~ -βa * S * Ia / Nₛ - βb * S * Ib / Nₛ,
        D(Ia) ~ βa * S * Ia / Nₛ - γa * Ia,
        D(Ib) ~ βb * S * Ib / Nₛ - γb * Ib,
        D(R) ~ γa * Ia + γb * Ib],
    t;
    name = :strains))
ngm_s = next_generation_matrix(strains, [Ia, Ib]; equilibrium = Dict(S => Nₛ, R => 0))
irreducible_blocks(ngm_s.K), basic_reproduction_number(ngm_s)
```

## Age structure: when there is no closed form

With `n ≥ 3` interacting groups the characteristic polynomial has no general closed-form
root, and `basic_reproduction_number` throws a `NoClosedFormError`. Parameter values then
give `R₀` numerically. Here we build an SIR model with three age groups and a contact
matrix `C`, using array symbolics.

```{julia}
@parameters q γ C[1:3, 1:3] Nᵢ[1:3]
@variables Sᵢ(t)[1:3] Iᵢ(t)[1:3]
Cm, Nv, Sv, Iv = collect(C), collect(Nᵢ), collect(Sᵢ), collect(Iᵢ)
λ = [q * sum(Cm[i, j] * Iv[j] / Nv[j] for j in 1:3) for i in 1:3]
age_eqs = [[D(Sv[i]) ~ -λ[i] * Sv[i] for i in 1:3];
           [D(Iv[i]) ~ λ[i] * Sv[i] - γ * Iv[i] for i in 1:3]]
age = complete(System(age_eqs, t; name = :age))
ngm_age = next_generation_matrix(age, Iv; equilibrium = Dict(Sv[i] => Nv[i] for i in 1:3))
ngm_age.K
```

```{julia}
try
    basic_reproduction_number(ngm_age)
catch err
    err
end
```

```{julia}
contacts = [10.0 3.0 1.0; 3.0 8.0 2.0; 1.0 2.0 4.0]     # contacts per day
sizes = [300.0, 500.0, 200.0]
vals = Dict{Any, Any}(Cm[i, j] => contacts[i, j] for i in 1:3, j in 1:3)
for i in 1:3
    vals[Nv[i]] = sizes[i]
end
vals[q] = 0.02
vals[γ] = 0.2
basic_reproduction_number(ngm_age, vals)
```

This agrees with the spectral radius of `q C / γ`, the familiar formula for a model with
frequency-dependent contacts:

```{julia}
maximum(abs, eigvals(0.02 .* contacts ./ 0.2))
```

Symbolic and numeric next-generation matrices are the same type, so everything
(states-at-infection, `K_L`, validation of sign conventions) works for both:

```{julia}
num = evaluate(ngm_age, vals)
(validate_decomposition(num), states_at_infection(num))
```
